about.title: Marina Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Losing a family member in a crash on a Marina street changes everything overnight — the grief, the funeral arrangements, the sudden gap in household income. Monterey County recorded 66 injury collisions and 1 traffic death in the most recent final crash year, a reminder that even a quiet coastal city like Marina sees serious wrecks, often clustering around Wednesday evenings between 5 and 7 p.m. near corridors such as Imjin Parkway and Reservation Road. California law gives surviving spouses, domestic partners, and children the first right to bring a wrongful death claim, with certain other dependents eligible if none of those relatives exist. These cases are separate from any criminal charges the responsible driver might face. LawProactive doesn't practice law — we simply listen to what happened and connect your family, free of charge, with an independent attorney who can explain your options and handle the legal work while you focus on each other.

whyChoose.title: Why Marina Families Reach Out to LawProactive

items.title: Who Can File Is Limited by Law
items.desc: California restricts standing to a spouse, domestic partner, or children first, then other dependents if none survive. An independent attorney can quickly confirm who in your family qualifies.

items.title: The Clock Starts at the Date of Death
items.desc: You generally have two years from the date of death to file, though claims against a government entity (like a public roadway defect) require faster action. Waiting too long can close off options entirely.

items.title: Recoverable Losses Go Beyond Bills
items.desc: California law allows recovery for funeral costs and lost financial support, but also for the loss of love, companionship, and guidance a family member provided — losses that are real even without a dollar sign attached.

items.question: How long do we have to file a wrongful death claim in Marina?
items.answer: In most cases, California gives you two years from the date of death to file a civil wrongful death claim. If the crash involved a government-maintained road or vehicle, the deadline is much shorter, so it helps to act sooner rather than later. An attorney can confirm the exact deadline once they understand the details of the collision.

items.question: Can our family file if the crash happened on a road like Reservation Road or Imjin Parkway?
items.answer: Yes — wrongful death claims can arise from crashes on any Marina roadway, whether it's a busy corridor like Reservation Road or a quieter side street. What matters is who was involved, how the crash happened, and who is legally eligible to file. An independent attorney can walk through those specifics with your family.

items.question: Is a wrongful death claim the same as a criminal case against the driver?
items.answer: No, they're separate. A criminal case is brought by the state and focuses on punishment, while a wrongful death claim is a civil case your family can bring to recover financial and personal losses. One can proceed even if the other doesn't result in charges or a conviction.

items.question: Does LawProactive charge anything to connect us with an attorney?
items.answer: No. LawProactive is a free service, and the attorneys in our network work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless there's a recovery. We're not a law firm ourselves — we simply help families in Marina get connected with someone who can advise them.
